hero.title: Employment agency in The Hague for <accent>hands-on work</accent>
hero.intro: We find people for window cleaning, cleaning, logistics, removals and construction and demolition in The Hague and the surrounding area. Job seekers and clients always speak to Jimmy or Lorenzo.

jobseeker.title: I am looking for work
jobseeker.body: View the open jobs or choose your occupation below.

employer.title: I am looking for staff
employer.body: Request people for a day, a few weeks or longer.

vacatures.title: The latest jobs
vacatures.accent: in The Hague and the surrounding area
vacatures.intro: Every job shows the gross hourly wage, the hours and the location. Applying takes a few minutes, even without a CV.
vacatures.emptyJobseeker: There are no jobs online right now. Register with us and we will call you as soon as there is work that suits you.

beroepen.title: Work and staff in
beroepen.intro: Choose an occupation and read what the work involves. Job seekers will find jobs and hourly wages, clients can read how to request people.

glazenwasser.body: Window cleaners clean windows, facades and solar panels, often at height from an aerial platform.

schoonmaker.body: Cleaners keep offices, schools, hotels and new homes clean, often early in the morning or in the evening.

logistiek-medewerker.body: Logistics workers pick orders, load and unload lorries and keep the warehouse in order.

verhuizer.body: Movers pack, carry furniture and set everything up again at the new address, for homes and offices.

hulpkracht-bouw-en-sloop.body: Construction and demolition labourers help skilled workers on site with carrying, clearing up and demolition work.

steps.title: From first contact to
steps.intro: Finding work and requesting staff at Groos takes three steps. That way everyone knows in advance what will happen.

steps.title: Apply or register
steps.body: Choose a job or register without one, you do not need a CV.

steps.title: We call you
steps.body: Jimmy or Lorenzo calls you to hear what work you are looking for and when you can work.

steps.title: You start
steps.body: If the work suits you, we agree your first working day, your hours and your hourly wage together.

steps.title: Request staff
steps.body: You tell us which people you need, from when and for how long.

steps.title: We propose people
steps.body: We discuss the work and the working hours with you and then propose people who fit.

steps.title: The work starts
steps.body: We stay in touch with you and the worker for as long as the assignment runs.

why.title: What you can
why.intro: We only promise what we can deliver. These are the fixed arrangements for everyone who works with Groos.

contactpersonen.title: Two dedicated contacts
contactpersonen.body: You always speak to Jimmy or Lorenzo. Their mobile numbers are on this site and with every job.

beroepen.title: Five hands-on occupations
beroepen.body: Groos focuses on window cleaning, cleaning, logistics, removals and construction and demolition. For each occupation this site explains what the work involves.

loon.title: Honest about pay
loon.body: Every job shows the gross hourly wage. By law a temporary worker receives the same pay as permanent colleagues in the same role.

solliciteren.title: Three ways to apply
solliciteren.body: Job seekers apply through the form, with a WhatsApp message or with a phone call. A CV is not needed.

people.title: At Groos you speak to
people.intro: They post the jobs, talk to job seekers and discuss requests with clients. Feel free to call or message them with a question about work or staff.

items.q: Does applying or registering cost money?
items.a: No, applying and registering are always free. Groos never asks for money for work, a contract or an application. If someone asks for it in our name, please report it to us.

items.q: Do I need a CV to apply?
items.a: No, you do not need a CV. You fill in a few details, such as your name and your phone number, and we discuss your experience on the phone.

items.q: Do I need to speak Dutch?
items.a: That depends on the job. Every job states whether you need Dutch for the work. You can also read this site in English.
Every job shows the gross hourly wage. By law you receive the same pay as permanent colleagues who do the same work. On top of that you build up holiday pay.

items.q: Will I get safety shoes and other protective equipment?
items.a: Yes, protective equipment such as safety shoes, gloves or a helmet is free if the work requires it. We tell you in advance what you need on your first working day.

items.q: What does a temporary worker cost?
items.a: The rate depends on the occupation, the number of hours, the working times and the length of the assignment. After your request we send you a proposal with an hourly rate.

items.q: For how long can I hire staff?
items.a: You decide, even if it is for a single day. We match the number of people and the hours to your planning.
You deal with Jimmy or Lorenzo, who handle your request themselves. Their numbers are on this site, so you can call them directly.

items.q: Do your people receive the same pay as my permanent staff?
items.a: Yes, the law requires equivalent pay. A temporary worker receives the same pay and the same allowances as your permanent staff in the same role. That is why we ask about pay at your company when you submit a request.

items.q: Who is responsible for safety at the workplace?
items.a: As the client you are responsible under the Working Conditions Act for a safe workplace and for explaining the work. We agree with you in advance which certificates and protective equipment are needed.

cta.title: One phone call is enough
cta.body: Call or message us on <link>{phone}</link>. If you would rather look around first, choose the route that suits you below.
